blocks.text: Ammonia behaves as a Bronsted-Lowry base by accepting a proton from an acid to form ammonium: NH3(aq) + H+(aq) gives NH4+(aq). It dissolves in water to form ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH), and an equilibrium is established between ammonia molecules and ammonium ions in the solution: NH3(aq) + H2O(l) in equilibrium with NH4+(aq) + OH-(aq), Kb = 1.8 x 10^-5. Ammonia solution is a weak base because of the low basicity constant and the equilibrium position lying far to the left.

blocks.title: Basicity constant Kb
blocks.text: Kb = [NH4+][OH-] / [NH3] = 1.8 x 10^-5 for ammonia in water; the small value means only a little of the dissolved ammonia is converted to ammonium and hydroxide ions.
